title: S3 bucket-quota permission can authorize bucket-policy modification
summary:
### Summary

A high-severity authorization-confusion vulnerability in SeaweedFS allows an S3 identity with only `s3:PutBucketQuota` permission to write an arbitrary bucket policy.

By combining the `policy` and `seaweedfs-quota` query subresources, authorization can be performed against `s3:PutBucketQuota` while the request is routed to `PutBucketPolicyHandler`. The validated exploit changed a private bucket's policy and exposed a private object to an unauthenticated user.

The issue was confirmed on SeaweedFS 4.47, commit `c5073360007d28385a33426a42ac3e4ec504c5a3`, and master commit `7643f4f5417680678de7529fd148f6099199db2c`.

Suggested severity: High, CVSS 3.1 8.1 (`AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`).

### Details

SeaweedFS uses separate data structures for request validation, IAM action resolution, and HTTP routing.

First, `operationSubresources` is intended to reject requests containing multiple operation-selecting query parameters. It contains `policy` but omits `seaweedfs-quota`:

https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/blob/7643f4f5417680678de7529fd148f6099199db2c/weed/s3api/s3api_path_validation.go#L42-L70

Consequently, the following request is not rejected as ambiguous:

```http
PUT /bucket?policy=&seaweedfs-quota=
```

Second, both query parameters appear in `bucketQueryActions`:

https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/blob/7643f4f5417680678de7529fd148f6099199db2c/weed/s3api/s3_action_resolver.go#L71-L124

The resolver iterates this Go map and returns the action associated with the first matching query parameter:

https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/blob/7643f4f5417680678de7529fd148f6099199db2c/weed/s3api/s3_action_resolver.go#L226-L235

Because Go map iteration order is unspecified, the combined request can be authorized as either `s3:PutBucketPolicy` or `s3:PutBucketQuota`.

Finally, the bucket-policy route is registered before the bucket-quota route:

https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/blob/7643f4f5417680678de7529fd148f6099199db2c/weed/s3api/s3api_server.go#L928-L933

https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/blob/7643f4f5417680678de7529fd148f6099199db2c/weed/s3api/s3api_server.go#L1023-L1028

Both routes match the combined query, but Gorilla mux selects the earlier `policy` route. When IAM resolves the request as `s3:PutBucketQuota`, a quota-only identity passes authorization while `PutBucketPolicyHandler` executes.

This violates the security invariant that the operation authorized by IAM must be the same operation selected by the router.

### PoC

#### Requirements

- SeaweedFS 4.47 or master commit `7643f4f5417680678de7529fd148f6099199db2c`
- `curl` with `--aws-sigv4` support
- `jq`
- A fresh, local data directory

The complete asserted PoC is included in `poc/poc.sh`. It records response bodies and exits nonzero if a control or exploit assertion fails.

#### Configuration

Save the following as `iam-config.json`. The attacker has only quota get/set permission on the test bucket. Advanced IAM is configured with default deny.

```json
{"identities":[{"name":"research-admin","credentials":[{"accessKey":"SWFS001ADMINKEY","secretKey":"SWFS001AdminSecretKeyLocalOnly"}],"actions":["Admin"]},{"name":"quota-operator","credentials":[{"accessKey":"SWFS001QUOTAKEY","secretKey":"SWFS001QuotaSecretKeyLocalOnly"}],"policyNames":["QuotaOnly"]}],"sts":{"issuer":"swfs001-local-research","signingKey":"U1dGUzAwMUxPQ0FMU0lHTklOR0tFWVNVUEBMSUVET05MWQ==","tokenDuration":"1h","maxSessionLength":"12h"},"policy":{"defaultEffect":"Deny","storeType":"memory"},"policies":[{"name":"QuotaOnly","document":{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Sid":"QuotaOnlyBoundary","Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:PutBucketQuota","s3:GetBucketQuota"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::swfs001-private"]}]}}],"roles":[],"providers":[]}
```

Start SeaweedFS in a researcher-controlled, loopback-only deployment:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/swfs001-data
/path/to/weed server -dir=/tmp/swfs001-data -...
